Tired of struggling to move AI apps from simple chat interfaces to secure, production-grade transactional workflows? 🛍️🤖

Anthropic just dropped `anthropics/commerce-agents`, a complete open-source blueprint providing production-grade reference architectures for building secure, dual-sided shopping and merchant AI agents using Claude. 

🔥 The Problem It Solves:
Architecting agent memory, safety fencing, and complex tool-calling loops from scratch eats up hundreds of hours. This repo solves the challenge by standardizing prompts, skills, tool contracts, and memory management across four runnable retail and service verticals: retail, travel, telecom, and entertainment.

✨ Key Features:
• Dual-Agent Architecture: Separate, role-specific agents for customer shopping and merchant operations.
• Multi-Runtime Support: Runs identically across the Anthropic Messages API, Claude Agent SDK, and hosted Managed Agents via MCP servers.
• Built-in Safety Fences: Strict provenance gates and human-approval workflows where merchant writes and checkouts are safely staged.
• Claude Code Plugin: Includes the `commerce-builder` CLI plugin to quickly scaffold and extend custom agents.

💡 Developer Value:
Map your existing systems—like Shopify, Stripe, or proprietary backends—to the standardized `StorefrontBackend` and `MerchantBackend` interfaces. You get secure, context-aware AI agents deployable across AWS Bedrock, GCP Vertex AI, and more, without writing custom boilerplate.

Ready to build the future of transactional commerce? Check out the repo and start building today:
https://github.com/anthropics/commerce-agents

Finally open up macOS's opaque 'System Data' black hole with a native Swift 6 menu bar app that lets you audit and purge disk bloat item-by-item. 🍏💻

If you are a macOS power user, iOS/macOS developer, or engineer juggling heavy package manager caches, you know the pain of mysteriously vanishing SSD space. macOS hides gigabytes of build artifacts, stale Xcode DerivedData, massive iOS simulator runtimes, abandoned package manager caches, and local APFS snapshots under the vague 'System Data' category. 

macos-sysdata is a native SwiftUI menu bar utility built to solve this exact problem by giving you item-by-item control instead of blind cache clearing. 

Key Features:
- Granular, Badge-Driven Item Classification: Every scanned item is tagged with a clear safety badge ('Safe' for auto-regrowing caches, 'Review' for items requiring manual attention, and 'Manual' for system-blocked paths), complete with idle-time tracking.
- Transparent Root Execution & CLI Integration: Privileged cleanup actions require individual osascript prompts where you can read the exact rm commands beforehand, alongside a --json flag for headless script integration.
- Intelligent Power-Down Lifecycle Management: Automatically detects and shuts down hanging iOS simulators during system shutdown to drastically accelerate userspace teardown times.
- Comprehensive Historical Auditing: Maintains a local scan history file that tracks growth, detects what files return after deletion, and surfaces which directories are silently eating up your storage.

Reclaim dozens of gigabytes on your space-constrained MacBook internal SSD today without risking system instability. 

Check it out on GitHub:
https://github.com/Jarvis322/macos-sysdata

Drop a star if you find it useful, and let us know in the comments how many gigabytes you managed to recover! 👇

Tired of spinning up heavy EVM archive nodes or writing fragile scrapers just to analyze prediction market data? 

Meet PolyLedger: an out-of-the-box Python CLI tool that bridges high-frequency Polymarket CLOB metadata and Polygon on-chain trades directly into a lightning-fast, locally queryable DuckDB file. 🚀

The Problem:
Building historical data environments or backtesting trading strategies on Polymarket usually means managing complex Postgres connection pools and dealing with messy, unnormalized Web3 trade legs. 

How PolyLedger Solves It:
It acts as a resumable data pipeline and indexer, aggregating market metadata from the CLOB API while streaming raw OrderFilled events from Polygon via Envio HyperSync. It decodes, structures, and writes both streams into a single local DuckDB database for instant analytical querying.

Key Features:
• Resumable & Idempotent: Commits rows and block cursors in single transactions with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING rules, ensuring interrupted runs resume seamlessly.
• Comprehensive Decoders: Handles both V1 and V2 Polymarket exchange layouts natively, normalizing distinct event signatures and side inferences.
• Zero-Server Columnar Storage: Leverages DuckDB for high-compression, zero-config queries, allowing seamless SQL joins over millions of trade rows alongside simple Parquet exports.
• Robust Network Resilience: Integrates Pydantic schema validation, exponential backoff with jitter, and shared token-bucket rate limiting.

Whether you are building a local backtesting environment for automated prediction market strategies, calculating VWAPs, or tracking whales via Jupyter notebooks, PolyLedger gets you set up in minutes.

Check out the repo and start querying:
https://github.com/nahrek/polyledger

As LLMs redefine discovery, how does your tech stack actually rank when developers ask AI for recommendations? 🤖

Traditional SEO is evolving, and if you are building in the AI era, you need to know how LLMs perceive your product versus your competitors. Enter NiubiGEO—the open-source analytics workbench designed to audit and track AI search engine visibility.

Here is the problem it solves: 
As search shifts to conversational interfaces, tracking visibility has become a guessing game. NiubiGEO automates testing against multiple LLMs via OpenRouter, evaluating how different models describe your domain, what competing products they surface, which keywords trigger brand mentions, and what underlying citations they reference.

Key Features Built for Developers & Growth Engineers:
- Multi-Model & Web Search Integration: Search, filter, and select arbitrary OpenRouter models while toggling native web search modes independently per test.
- Isolated Project Workspaces: Manage multiple product domains with strict separation of configurations, historical runs, and evidence without data bleeding.
- Keyword Testing Without Brand Bias: Measure whether your product appears organically when users search category terms without mentioning your brand name.
- Comprehensive Evidence & Citation Logging: Store original model outputs, provider citations, and answer URLs to allow manual auditing and reproducible checks.

Whether you are a developer advocate or technical founder, you can easily self-host via Docker or Node.js to programmatically monitor how models perceive your documentation, APIs, and product positioning over time. Stop guessing and start measuring your AI footprint.

👉 Check out the repo and self-host your own workbench:
https://github.com/Albert-Weasker/niubigeo

🎮 Bridging vendor divides, this open project implements a custom HIP-based neural network runtime to bring DLSS 5 Neural Rendering to AMD Radeon RX 7000 and 9000 series GPUs!

Are you tired of vendor lock-in holding back advanced graphics tech? Danielblnc/DLSS-NR-on-AMD solves this by delivering a clean-room, ground-up reimplementation of the neural network runtime optimized specifically for AMD GPU architectures. It allows games utilizing FSR to route and process DLSS 5 Neural Rendering payloads on AMD hardware without relying on native NVIDIA-specific hardware blocks or runtime translation layers.

🔥 Key Features to Explore:
• Native AMD HIP kernels and custom memory layouts built from the ground up
• Seamless DirectX 12 hooks that map FSR game pipelines to execute neural rendering routines
• Built-in configurable in-game overlay for granular runtime tweaks like mode adjustment (inline/async), tone intensity, and structural controls
• Modular update and removal tooling packaged via an automated setup executable

For graphics programmers, reverse engineers, and game developers, this repo is a goldmine. It serves as an exceptional case study in cross-architecture compute optimization, custom runtime writing, and API interception. Whether you want to study custom HIP kernel implementations or experiment with hardware-agnostic neural network runtimes in real-time pipelines, this codebase offers massive architectural value.

Check out the repository and dive into the source code here:
https://github.com/Danielblnc/DLSS-NR-on-AMD
